title: What to Wear to an Indian Wedding in Winter (Guest Outfit Guide)
excerpt: A simple guide for wedding guests in cold weather – the best fabrics, outfit ideas for every function, layering tips and what to avoid.
body:
Invited to an Indian wedding between November and February? Evening functions can get cold, especially in North India, the UK, Canada and the USA. Here is how to dress beautifully and stay warm.

## The best fabrics for a winter wedding

- **Velvet** – warm, rich and perfect for evening functions.
- **Silk and brocade** – structured and festive, good for day functions.
- **Wool-blend shawls and pashmina** – the easiest way to add warmth over any outfit.

Avoid very light chiffon or cotton for outdoor evening functions unless you add a warm layer.

## Outfit ideas for every function

| Function | What to wear | Why it works |
|---|---|---|
| Mehndi (day) | Bright cotton-silk or printed kurta set | Light and easy to sit in |
| Sangeet (evening) | Velvet Anarkali with organza dupatta | Twirls well and keeps you warm |
| Wedding ceremony | Silk or velvet suit in a jewel tone | Rich, traditional and photo-ready |
| Reception | Velvet kurta with brocade palazzo | Regal and comfortable for long evenings |

For more choices by function – haldi to reception – see our [Anarkali suits for weddings](/collections/anarkali-suits/).

## How to layer without hiding your outfit

- Drape a **pashmina or wool shawl** over the shoulders – it looks elegant in photos too.
- Wear a **long coat** to and from the venue and take it off for pictures.
- Add **skin-tone thermals** under a lined velvet kurta – nobody will know.
- Choose **closed juttis or heels** for outdoor lawns.

## Two climates: cold outside, heated hall inside

Abroad, most winter Indian weddings – in Brampton, Surrey, New Jersey, Leicester or Melbourne's winter – happen in large banquet halls, hotels, gurdwaras and mandirs. They are well heated, and with a few hundred guests on the dance floor they get warm fast. The common mistake is to choose a heavy outfit to fight the cold, then overheat all evening.

So keep the heavy warmth in layers you can take off:

| Layer | What to choose | Tip |
|---|---|---|
| Base | Thin thermal leggings and a fitted thermal top | Skin tone or black; avoid thick fleece |
| Outfit | Anarkali or kurta set with three-quarter or full sleeves | Velvet for a seated reception; georgette, chiffon or embroidered cotton if you will dance for hours |
| Warmth | Pashmina, wool shawl or a cropped faux-fur stole | For outdoor photos and the gurdwara |
| Outerwear | Long parka or wool coat that covers your hem | Leave it at the coat check on arrival |
| Feet | Insulated, waterproof boots | Change into juttis or heels inside |

Fold the dupatta into a tote rather than stuffing it into a coat sleeve, so it stays crease-free. ## Snow, salt and shoes

- **Boots to the door, shoes inside.** Carry juttis or heels in a bag and change in the lobby.
- **Mind your hem.** Slush and road salt leave white marks. Lift your Anarkali when you cross a car park, or tuck it under your coat.
- **Hand warmers in your coat pocket** help during an outdoor baraat.
- **Lip balm and hand cream:** heated halls and winter air are very drying.
- **At a gurdwara** you leave your shoes at the entrance, so warm socks under your pants keep your feet comfortable on cold floors.

## Not every wedding abroad is a winter one

Summer weddings in Canada, the USA and the UK – June to August – can be genuinely hot, with outdoor mehndis and backyard sangeets. Then switch to breathable cotton and kota doria; the [navy blue kota doria embroidered kurta set](/products/navy-blue-kota-doria-embroidered-kurta-pant-dupatta-set/) is airy but still elegant for an evening event. In Australia, December to February is summer, so see our [Australia wedding guide](/blog/what-to-wear-to-an-indian-wedding-in-australia/) instead.

## What not to wear

- White or all-black at some traditional ceremonies – check with the hosts first. Black with gold, like our velvet set, is usually perfect for receptions and parties.
- Outfits heavier than the bride's.
- Very high heels on grass or sand.

## Frequently asked questions

**What should a guest wear to an Indian wedding in winter?**
A velvet or silk suit in a jewel tone, with a shawl or long coat for outdoor functions.

**Can I wear black to an Indian wedding?**
Black is usually fine for receptions, sangeet and parties, especially with gold details. For the main ceremony, a bright jewel tone is a safer choice.

**Is velvet too hot for an indoor wedding?**
A lined velvet Anarkali is comfortable at most indoor receptions, and a light organza dupatta keeps the look airy. If you plan to dance for hours in a packed, heated hall, a georgette or chiffon Anarkali with a warm shawl may feel better.

**How do I protect my outfit from snow and salt?**
Wear a long coat that covers your hem, lift your Anarkali when crossing slushy areas, and change into your indoor shoes at the venue.

**How early should I order my outfit from abroad?**
At least 4 weeks before the wedding for a ready size and 5 weeks for custom fit, to allow for making, dispatch and delivery.
